title: MECH_02 ESQUIVA emits no CueEliminated feedback on player elimination
description: Surfaced by dev-t101 during the TASK-058 L2 fix (grep-confirmed): the V2 EsquivaMicrogame declares a CueEliminated feedback cue but NEVER emits it via EmitFeedback on a player elimination — unlike Reacciona, which emits its feedback cues. So when a player is eliminated in ESQUIVA, no feedback cue reaches the View/HUD/FeedbackController layer (the elimination flash/juice the feedback system exists to drive). Scoring/ranking is correct and unaffected (elimination tick is recorded in the result) — this is purely the missing feedback-cue emission. Left out of TASK-058's 'test + doc only' fix round as out-of-scope. WORK: emit CueEliminated (with the eliminated seat) at the elimination site in EsquivaMicrogame.Tick, mirroring how the other v2 mechanics emit their cues; add a feedback-trace test pinning that an elimination emits exactly one CueEliminated for the right seat (mirror Reacciona's feedback-trace lock). Cross-check the other v2 mechanics for the same declared-but-unemitted gap while here. Coordinates with TASK-027 (StagePresenter/View) which consumes these cues — but the emission itself is Core-side and fast-testable.
acceptance_criteria: EsquivaMicrogame emits CueEliminated (naming the eliminated seat) at each elimination, consistent with how the other v2 mechanics emit feedback cues.
A fast-suite feedback-trace test pins that a player elimination emits exactly one CueEliminated for the correct seat, and that no elimination emits none (non-vacuous).
The other v2 mechanics are checked for the same declared-but-unemitted cue gap; any found is fixed here or ticketed.
Fast suite green; no change to scoring/ranking behavior (determinism + zero-alloc pins from TASK-058 stay green).
